tagline: Up the North Yuba, through the gold camps of 1849.
intro: Out of Yuba County, Highway 49 crosses into Sierra County and keeps to the canyon of the North Yuba River, in Tahoe National Forest. Goodyears Bar comes first, then Downieville at the forks, then Sierra City under the Sierra Buttes. Past Bassetts it climbs to Yuba Pass, 6,710 feet up on the divide between the North Yuba and the Middle Fork of the Feather River.

This is the Golden Chain Highway, laid through the mining camps of the 1849 gold rush. Downieville had fifteen hotels by 1850 and more than 5,000 people the year after. It kept going as the county seat.

moments.title: Goodyears Bar
moments.text: Slaughter's Bar until 1851, renamed for the Goodyear brothers, who found gold on the North Yuba here in 1849 with two partners and built themselves a cabin.

moments.title: Downieville
moments.text: First called The Forks, for the meeting of the Downie River and the North Yuba, it was in the running for state capital in 1853.

moments.title: Sierra City
moments.text: Highway 49 is the main street, the Sierra Buttes tower over it, and in 1869 the mines near town gave up a gold nugget of more than 106 pounds.
